en: The Amoghapāśa-Vairocana-Buddha-Mahābhiṣeka-Raśmi-Mantra, one fascicle;
excerpted from the twenty-eight fascicles of the Amoghapāśa Sūtra.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daixingshan Monastery—who held the rank of Kaifu Yitongsan Si, Teci, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Suku with a fief of three thousand households, was invested with purple robes, posthumously granted the title of Sikong, and conferred the honorific title of Dajian Zhenghao Daguangzhi—by Imperial Decree: Oṃ ā-mu-ga-vi-ru-za-na-sva-ra-saṃbhava-hūṃ. Tathāgata Vairocana.
This is the Chapter on the Method of the Mother Dhāraṇī Seal Samaya Supernatural Power,
which is the foremost of all.
If there are any past transgressions, such as the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, or the four grave offenses, [this shall purify them].
It will be completely extinguished like ashes.
If there are sentient beings who,
wherever they may be, hear this Great Consecration Light Mantra, [it shall likewise be extinguished].
If those who have heard this [mantra] twenty-three times pass it through their faculty of hearing,
they shall immediately attain the eradication of all karmic obstacles.
Even if sentient beings have committed all manner of offenses— the ten unwholesome paths of action, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave transgressions— [they shall be purified].
It is as if fine dust were to fill this entire world;
yet, upon the dissolution of the body and the end of life, one would fall into the various evil realms.
By consecrating earth or sand one hundred and eight times with this mantra, [the same result is achieved].
One should scatter [the powder] upon the scattered remains of deceased persons in a śītavana (cemetery),
or scatter it upon graves; wherever one encounters such places, one should scatter it there.
Those who have passed away—
whether among the denizens of hell, or among the hungry ghosts,
or among the asuras, or among the animals.

By the power of the empowerment of the mantra of the Great Consecration Light of the True Original Vow of all the Non-empty Tathāgatas and the Non-empty Vairocana Tathāgata, and by the force of the empowered sand and earth.
At that moment, they immediately attained radiance and the purification of their bodies from all karmic retributions for past sins; casting off their suffering bodies,
they proceeded to the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the western direction,
where they were born by transformation within lotus flowers and shall never again fall until they attain bodhi.
Furthermore, there are sentient beings who, for years on end and months at a time,
suffer from the wasting disease of jaundice and myriad forms of affliction;
such patients are the karmic retribution of their past lives.
By reciting this mantra one thousand and eighty times daily in a loud voice before the patient for one, two, or three days,
the obstacles of illness resulting from past karma will be eliminated.
If one is tormented by a ghost such that the soul-consciousness becomes distressed and confused, losing one's voice and remaining mute,
the mantra-holder should empower their hand one hundred and eight times and then rub it over the person's head and face.
Place the hand upon the heart and the forehead;
by performing the empowerment one thousand and eighty times, one will be cured.
It can also cure and dispel those who cause illness and affliction, such as the deity Mahākāla,
as well as diseases caused by various ghosts, spirits, and malevolent demons.
Consecrate a cord of five-colored threads with one hundred and eight knots,
and tie it around the waist, arms, and neck of the patient.
Then the illness will be cured.
If one has various types of malarial fevers,
one should empower a white cord with one hundred and eight knots.
Tie it around one's neck or wear it as an empowered garment,
and the illness will be immediately cured.
If one consecrates stone sweet flag (achyranthes) one hundred and eighty times and chews it while conversing with another,
one will prevail over and subdue them.
If one uses powdered substances such as black pepper, tagara incense,
blue sandalwood, small juniper, yellow sandalwood,
and rasajāna (which in the language of Tang means the juice of small juniper), in appropriate quantities;
Make water-taming pills the size of jujube fruits;
perform one hundred thousand recitations of empowerment over them,
then dry them in the shade.
If one suffers from any illness caused by ghosts or spirits,
various types of malaria, poisoning, or loss of voice,
one should grind the medicine with water.
Perform the empowerment one hundred and eight times.
Dot the two eyes, the forehead, and the heart with [the substance] while maintaining a wrathful empowerment.
Then the illness will be cured.
If the spirit causing the illness does not release the person,
their head shall split open like the branches of an *ari* tree.
If one is stung by various venomous insects, snakes, or scorpions, applying this medicine to the eyes will cause the affliction to be immediately cured.
Furthermore, there is another method: using fresh rice husks (*śāli-tuṣa*).
Having bathed for purification and put on clean garments,
grind the medicine with water;
empower it one hundred and eight times and apply it to the eyes of the *mīḍhala* rice.
If one performs the wrathful empowerment (krodhādhiṣṭhāna) one hundred and eight times,
the [deity] will immediately rise from its seat and answer all questions.
If one wishes to release it:
Consecrate white mustard seed water twenty-one times and scatter it over the parched rice;
it will immediately return to its former state.
If one is invited by a person of noble rank,
one should apply this medicine to the eyes before going to see them;
then they will treat one with mutual respect and hospitality.
The One-Scroll Amoghapāśa-Vairocana-Buddha-Mahābhiṣeka-Raśmi-Mantra.
